{!Contact.FirstName}, Thank you for your interest in the Master of Science in Human Nutrition at Arizona State University! I look forward to assisting you as you consider your options at ASU.
About the Program
The primary objective of the graduate program in Human Nutrition is to provide advanced training in the research methodologies and biochemical laboratory skills that are relevant to nutrition. Graduate students are expected to develop competencies in research methods and in advanced practice knowledge relevant to their area of study. The skills and knowledge acquired during the course of training should enable each student to develop professional competencies that can be applied to significant problems and issues within the field of nutrition and dietetics.
The MS degree is aimed at two categories of students:
Students who want to become Registered Dietitians with the MS degree: The majority of applicants in teh ASU MS in Human Nutrition program plan on completing the combined two-year MS degree, plus Dietetic Internship (DI) before taking the RD exam. Only students who have completed an accredited Didactic Program in Dietetics (DPD) are eligible for the combined MS/DI option.
Applications to the ASU MS/DI program for fall only have a deadilne of February 15.
Applications to the ASU/VA MS/DI program for spring only have a deadline of September 25.
Learn more about the MS in Human Nutrition with optional Dietetic Internship
Students who want to complete an MS degree in Nutrition only, without the RD credential: Less than 10% of students who wish to complete this MS degree without the dietetic internship are admitted each year – usually in order to go on to a PhD program or apply to medical school. It is highly recommended that studetns have undergraduate degrees in nutrition or science to be a competitive applicant. Students can complete only the MS degree without the dietetic internship in approximately one year depending upon successful completion of their research thesis.
The priority application deadline is February 15; however, applications will be considered for fall admission until June 15 on a space available basis.
About Admission
We seek applicants with strong GRE scores on all portions of the exam. However, there are no minimum scores for the GRE examination, which is evaluated in the context of your entire application package.
International student information is found on the Graduate Admissions webpage.
Tuition and fee information can be calculated according to your residency and degree program.
Please let me know if you have any questions and thank you so much for your interest!
